rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (ki 0.10, kp 2.4, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.2) scored 679.43. Oval finished 20/20 (mean 1.83 s) and s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.14 s), so the integral term did not cause windup. The slalom still ended 0/20 off track, with mean max_error 0.0634 (above the 0.06 m limit) and 1.0 line-loss events per run. Its progress was 0.32. Across iterations 3 to 7, slalom max_error stayed between 0.0618 and 0.0646 under every controller tried. Changing kp, kd and ki did not move it below 0.06. The Evaluator's decision rule for this case says to return to the best controller (kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05, iteration 5, 699.16) and then widen sensor coverage. Iteration 1 showed that wider x coverage cut s-bend line losses from 2.05 to 1.15 and slalom losses from 1.75 to 1.05, so coverage is the lever with the most evidence that has not yet been tested at the current y.

Changes. (1) Controller returns to iteration 5: kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, line_loss last_direction. The ki 0.1 test gave no benefit and this is the best-scoring controller. (2) Sensor x positions widen from plus or minus 0.03 m to plus or minus 0.04 m: -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04, with y 0.06 kept. The sensor footprint stays at 16 mm and sensor_weights stay at [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. Wheel geometry, mass and body are unchanged.

Expected result. Slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0.8 or below, and slalom max_error drops below about 0.06 so that some slalom runs can finish. Oval and s-bend should stay at 20/20 or near it. The signal scale is unchanged, but the reading-weighted average now has more lateral reach, so recovery from larger offsets should improve.

Hypotheses and measurements. (a) Wider coverage reduces slalom line losses, which are the path to max_error under 0.06. (b) The score holds at about 699 or better if oval and s-bend stay at 1.0 finish rate. Measurements requested: the full set, read per track, with emphasis on slalom max_error, line_loss_events, completion, and steering_oscillation on s-bend. If slalom line losses fall but the robot still goes off track, the next step is a small kd change. If the oval or s-bend finish rate drops below 0.95, return to the sensor positions at plus or minus 0.03 m.
